voiceover: And there's one more thing the data can't capture. Skimpflation. Same package, same size, same price — but cheaper ingredients. Thinner chips. Waterier ice cream. Less cocoa in the chocolate. Unlike shrinkflation, there's no government data series for this. No BLS measurement. It's real — economists acknowledge it — but it lives in the gap between what statistics can track and what your taste buds notice. <break time="500ms"/> If you were shopping during this decade, it probably didn't FEEL like things were getting cheaper. And in one sense, they weren't — per trip to the store. You were buying the same number of packages, paying roughly the same at checkout, getting less in the bag each time, and sometimes getting a lesser product too. The per-unit math works out. The grocery receipt doesn't care about per-unit math. <break time="1000ms"/> The lines are drifting down. Everything looks calm.

visual.description: Phase 1 (~30s): Skimpflation concept visual. Three identical product cards side by side — same package icon, same size label, same price tag. But a subtle indicator shows degrading quality: stars/quality bar going from 5→4→3. Text label: 'SKIMPFLATION' in Montserrat Bold 48px, Muted Pink, centered above. Below: 'Same package. Cheaper ingredients. No data series.' in Inter 20px, Accent Cream. Phase 2 (~25s): Transition back to the race chart at 2019 showing the downward-drifting lines — now with a subtle question mark overlay at 30% opacity, suggesting the data may not tell the full story. Phase 3 (~15s): Chart holds still. 'The lines are drifting down. Everything looks calm.' — ominous still frame before Act 3.

notes: Longest scene in Act 2 — 70 seconds. Needs clear phase transitions to avoid visual monotony. Phase 1 (skimpflation concept, 0–30s) uses the Remotion component style — no chart, just clean graphic design. Phase 2 (30–55s) transitions BACK to the race chart — crossfade over 8 frames. Phase 3 (55–69.67s) is the ominous hold. The 1000ms break before the final sentence is where the question mark overlay should pulse. The final line 'Everything looks calm' should feel unsettling — a calm before the storm. Film grain 3%.
